definitions.explanation: An alcoholic beverage made from fermented grapes. The traditional Japanese word for wine, though ワイン (from English 'wine') is now more commonly used in everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: ぶどう{酒|しゅ}を{一杯|いっぱい}{飲|の}む。
examples.english: To have a glass of wine.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}いぶどう{酒|しゅ}が{好|す}きだ。
この{地方|ちほう}は{昔|むかし}からぶどう{酒|しゅ}の{産地|さんち}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: This region has long been known as a wine-producing area.

notes: Compound of ぶどう (grapes) + {酒|しゅ} (alcohol/liquor). Also written as {葡萄酒|ぶどうしゅ} with kanji. In modern Japanese, ワイン is far more common in everyday conversation; ぶどう{酒|しゅ} appears more in literary, formal, or traditional contexts. The {酒|しゅ} suffix is used for other types of alcohol as well: {日本酒|にほんしゅ} (sake), {梅酒|うめしゅ} (plum wine), {焼酎|しょうちゅう} (distilled spirit). Japan's main wine-producing region is {山梨県|やまなしけん} (Yamanashi Prefecture).
